chief_complaint: chronic back/shoulder pain and grooving from bra straps
hpi_details: A 59-year-old female presents with chronic back and shoulder pain and bra-strap grooving related to large breasts. Symptoms have persisted despite supportive garments and conservative measures.
ideas: She thinks the heavy weight of her chest has pulled her upper spine out of alignment and pinched nerves in her neck.
concerns: She is worried that the chronic strain will permanently damage her spine and stop her from lifting and playing with her grandchildren.
expectations: She hopes to obtain a clinical referral and documentation to get breast reduction surgery covered by insurance.

history.answer: My breasts are so heavy that my upper back and shoulders ache constantly, and my bra straps dig painful grooves right into my shoulders.
I have always had large breasts, but the aching in my neck, shoulders, and upper back has become steadily worse over the past five years.
The pain is spread across both shoulders, the back of my neck, and between my shoulder blades down my upper back.
It feels like a constant, dull, heavy ache, as if I have been carrying a weighted backpack all day. On busy days, it reaches about a six or seven out of ten.
The aching is there almost every day from morning until night, and it has gradually become harder to bear as the years have gone by.
Standing or walking for a long time makes it much worse, as does wearing tight bras or carrying groceries.
Lying flat on my back relieves some of the tension, and taking off my bra relieves the strap pressure, though the heavy pulling remains.
Yes, my bra straps leave deep, indented grooves across the tops of both shoulders that stay red, sore, and tender even after I take the bra off.
During warm weather or after sweating, the skin under both breasts becomes red, itchy, and irritated, though I use powder to keep it dry.
No, the skin has never broken open, blistered, bled, or had any foul-smelling drainage.
Sometimes my fingers feel slightly tingly when the straps press hard on my shoulders, but I have no constant numbness or weakness in my arms.
No, I check my breasts regularly and have not felt any lumps, hardness, or focal changes in either breast.
No, I have never had any fluid leaking from my nipples, and they have not pulled inward.
No, I have not had any fevers, chills, or night sweats.
My weight has been completely stable around one hundred and forty pounds for the past several years.
I bought specialty wide-strap bras, supportive sports bras, and completed four months of physical therapy for neck and core strengthening, but none of it provided lasting relief.
I take over-the-counter ibuprofen or acetaminophen once or twice a week when it gets intense, but it only dulls the ache for a few hours.
My primary care doctor examined my spine and shoulders two years ago and said the spine looked fine and the ache was chronic muscular strain from breast weight.
I get routine screening mammograms every one to two years. My last one was about ten months ago, and the results were completely normal.
It limits my life quite a bit. I cannot jog or do aerobic exercise because the bouncing causes too much pain, and doing household chores leaves my back exhausted.
history.topic: Impact on daily activities and exercise

history.answer: It is difficult to find a comfortable position to sleep, especially on my side or stomach, because of the pressure and pull on my chest and neck.
I think the sheer weight pulling down on my chest has bent my spine and pinched nerves in my neck and shoulders.
I'm so worried that my neck and spine are getting ruined to the point where I won't be able to hold my grandkids.
I have no chronic medical conditions, no high blood pressure, no asthma, and no diabetes.
I have never had any surgeries, and I have never been hospitalized.
I do not take any daily prescription medications, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medicines, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco. I drink one glass of wine socially once or twice a month.
I work part-time as an office receptionist and live with my husband in an apartment.
My mother and older sister also had very large breasts and struggled with upper back pain, but there is no family history of breast cancer.
I went through menopause naturally eight years ago when I was fifty-one, and I have not had any bleeding since.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 68 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.6°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Well-nourished, comfortable female appearing stated age in no acute distress.
Deep bilateral shoulder grooving from bra straps with hyperpigmentation; mild inframammary erythema without maceration, erosion, or purulence.
Bilateral prominent breast hypertrophy with severe ptosis; no discrete masses, skin dimpling, or nipple retraction; no axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Symmetric chest wall expansion without tenderness; no palpable chest wall deformities.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally on auscultation without wheezing, crackles, or rhonchi.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs.
Mild tenderness to palpation over the bilateral trapezius, rhomboid, and paracervical musculature; no midline spinal tenderness; full spinal range of motion.
Intact motor strength (5/5) symmetrically throughout bilateral upper extremities, including shoulder abduction, elbow flexion/extension, and hand grip.
Intact light touch and pinprick sensation symmetrically across bilateral upper extremities and cervical dermatomes without focal deficit.
